content.title: About
content.content: Chickpeas are a legume widely used in cooking. Canned chickpeas with added fat are a ready‑to‑eat product packed in glass or metal cans. The added fat (usually vegetable oil) enhances flavor and texture.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Chickpeas are also known as garbanzo beans in many regions.
Canning allows chickpeas to be stored for several years without significant nutrient loss.
Added fat improves the absorption of fat‑soluble vitamins such as vitamin E.
Chickpeas are a major source of plant protein for vegetarian and vegan diets.
In some countries canned chickpeas are used as a base for traditional dishes like hummus.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: Chickpeas provide about 19 g of protein per 100 g, making them a valuable plant‑based protein source.

items.title: High in fiber
items.content: Dietary fiber supports healthy digestion and promotes satiety.

items.title: Source of iron and folate
items.content: Iron is essential for blood formation, while folate is important for cell division.

items.title: Contains healthy fats
items.content: The added vegetable oil supplies monounsaturated and polyunsaturated fatty acids beneficial for heart health.

items.title: Low glycemic index
items.content: Chickpeas raise blood sugar slowly, which helps with glucose control.

items.title: Legume allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to chickpeas.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Canned chickpeas often contain added salt; people monitoring sodium intake should choose low‑salt versions.

items.title: Higher calorie density due to fat
items.content: Added fat increases the product’s caloric value; portion control is advisable.

items.title: Bacterial contamination if packaging is damaged
items.content: Compromised cans can harbor pathogens; such products should be discarded.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Canned chickpeas can be eaten straight from the can, added to salads, soups, stews, blended into hummus, or used in vegetarian patties. It is recommended to drain the liquid and, if desired, rinse the chickpeas before use.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store unopened cans in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. After opening, keep the chickpeas in a sealed container in the refrigerator and consume within 3–4 days.
